subject: Cloud procurement feasibility — marketplace vs PO (next steps)
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@finovate.com>
To: alex_martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Intro + procurement context after today's demo

Alex / Marissa — thanks for the demo today, really helpful. Quick recap from our side and a few ask items so we can move towards procurement: 

- Finovate Payments is evaluating Redwood for payment NLP (transaction classification + semantic search) across a subset of our merchant data. We'll start with a 12-month committed pilot. 
- Primary procurement constraint: our central procurement team requires either a PO (NET30 invoicing) or purchase via AWS Marketplace private offer. Corporate card is only allowed for <$5k purchases. 
- We need: (1) a commercial quote showing annual committed price, (2) confirmation of Marketplace private offer capability and whether price parity applies, and (3) a short timeline for Marketplace listing / private offer setup (if applicable). 

Attaching our standard procurement form (we'll need your company details, W-9, and invoice remit info).

Attachment: Finovate_Procurement_Form.pdf (stub)

Can you confirm the best route (PO invoice vs Marketplace private offer) given Redwood's platform options and whether there are any gating technical or ops items? Also please confirm who in your billing/legal team I should loop in.

Thanks — Sam
Samantha Lee
Head of Vendor Programs
Finovate Payments
From: alex_martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@finovate.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + procurement context after today's demo

Sam — great to meet you (and congrats on the buyer protection flow you showed). High level on options and what we'll need from Finovate to scope the commercial path: 

Marketplace vs PO (short):
- AWS/GCP/Azure Marketplace: we support private offers on AWS Marketplace and private/offers-equivalent on GCP (Cloud Marketplace Private Offers). Azure has a longer listing path but we can do invoice/PO through standard procurement. Time to private-offer availability: 2–4 weeks from signed private offer + marketplace onboarding (typical).
- PO / Direct invoicing: we can issue NET30 invoices if you have a PO number; our finance ops will do monthly or annual invoices depending on the commitment.
- Card: only feasible for small initial pilot under $5k as you mentioned.

Decision criteria I recommend you validate with procurement/legal:
1) Do you require purchase via marketplace for billing traceability or compliance?
2) Do you need price parity (same price on marketplace) or are private offer discounts acceptable?
3) Is a reseller/partner required for Marketplace Private Offers in your account?

To move:
- I attached a short factsheet that outlines marketplace timelines and the differences in invoicing and entitlements.
- Draft quote attached for the 12-month committed pilot so procurement has a starting number. If you prefer a marketplace private offer we will convert the quote to the PO/offer flow and share the private-offer draft.

Attachments: RWI_AWS_Marketplace_Factsheet.pdf, RWI_Quote_Draft_Finovate_2027.xlsx (stubs)

Next steps I propose: 
- You confirm procurement's preference (private offer vs direct PO) and the remit/billing contacts (we need remit address, tax ID, PO contact).
- If private offer: we schedule a 30-minute onboarding with our marketplace ops (I can bring in Dev Patel to cover technical/metering questions).
- If PO: provide PO template and we will route to finance for NET30 invoice terms.

Looping in Marissa to coordinate legal/contract redline expectations.

— Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Procurement Team <procurement@finovate.com>

Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + procurement context after today's demo

Alex / Marissa — following up from Sam's note. A couple specifics from procurement: 

- Finovate requires NET30 invoicing on a PO for all multi-month vendor commitments unless purchase is through AWS Marketplace private offer (private offers accepted).
- Marketplace private offer is preferable for us because it ties to our cloud billing and simplifies internal chargebacks; however, we need the private offer to be issued to our AWS account and show the discounted committed price.
- Required docs for routing: W-9, sample invoice, reseller certificate (if applicable), and a signed MSA or private-offer terms.

We can target getting a PO ready in ~7 business days after we receive the finalized quote + standard vendor docs. For a marketplace private offer, we need an internal owner for onboarding and a contact who will accept the offer in the AWS console.

Procurement contact: procurement@finovate.com (use that address for vendor docs).

Thanks — Finovate Procurement
